---
title: Using rpix with an IDE
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    collapse: true
    comment: '#>'
---

Most R users work in an IDE rather than a terminal: RStudio, Positron or VS Code. Install the IDE as usual; most IDEs aren't available as conda packages, or not in recent versions. Then let rpix point it at the R in your project's Pixi environment, when you set the project up:

```r
rpix::use_pixi(ide = "positron")
```

or later, for one IDE at a time, with `use_pixi_rstudio()`, `use_pixi_positron()` or `use_pixi_vscode()`.

Whichever IDE you use, `rpix::pixi_sitrep()` checks that it runs the project's R, and suggests fixes if it doesn't.

## Positron

### Set up

```r
rpix::use_pixi_positron()
```

This turns on Positron's discovery of R in Pixi environments, in the project's `.vscode/settings.json`.

### Every day

In Positron's interpreter picker, pick **R (Pixi: default)**: the R from the project's default environment. Positron remembers it for the project, and starts it whenever you open the project. It activates the environment when it starts R, on Windows too.

### Another environment

Each of the project's environments is listed as its own R, e.g. **R 4.4.3 (Pixi: r44)**. Pick it in the interpreter picker.

### If something's off

- **Positron starts another R.** Positron prefers the R you last used in the project. If you used another R there before setting up Pixi, pick **R (Pixi: default)** once.
- **R (Pixi: default) isn't listed.** Positron may still show the R installations it found before. Run **Interpreter: Discover All Interpreters** from the Command Palette. Restart Positron if you've only just turned on discovery.

## RStudio

### Set up

```r
rpix::use_pixi_rstudio()
```

This adds an `rstudio` task to `pixi.toml`, and creates an `.Rproj` file if the project doesn't have one.

### Every day

Start RStudio with the task, in a terminal in the project folder:

```sh
pixi run rstudio
```

RStudio picks its R when it starts, so it has to be started this way. The task starts a new RStudio even if one is already running, and opens the project.

On Windows, the task expects RStudio in `C:/Program Files/RStudio`. If it's somewhere else, change the path in `pixi.toml`.

### Another environment

```sh
pixi run --environment test rstudio
```

This works for environments that include the default feature, which the task belongs to.

### If something's off

- **RStudio uses another R.** You probably opened the project another way, e.g. by double-clicking the `.Rproj` file. Close RStudio and use `pixi run rstudio`.

## VS Code

### Set up

```r
rpix::use_pixi_vscode()
```

This adds the languageserver package to the environment, and points the [R extension](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=REditorSupport.r) at the environment's R, in the project's `.vscode/settings.json`. It works the same in VSCodium.

When the R extension offers to install its sess package, accept: it installs into the environment.

### Every day

Open the project folder in VS Code. The R extension uses the environment's R, and the project's `.Rprofile` activates the environment.

On Windows, the environment's R only starts when the environment is activated, because it needs the environment's `Library\bin` folder on the `PATH`. So start VS Code from the project's environment:

```sh
pixi run code .
```

### Another environment

Change `r.executablePath` and `r.consolePath` in `.vscode/settings.json` to the environment's R, e.g. `${workspaceFolder}/.pixi/envs/r44/bin/R`, and reload the window. On Windows, start VS Code with `pixi run --environment r44 code .`.

### If something's off

- **The R extension can't find R.** Check that the environment is installed (`pixi install`), and that the paths in `.vscode/settings.json` exist.

## The message at startup

If you start R in a Pixi project with an R that isn't from the project's environment, e.g. by double-clicking the `.Rproj` file, which opens your usual R, the project's `.Rprofile` says so, as long as rpix is installed in that R:

```
! This R isn't from the project's Pixi environment, so it doesn't use the project's packages.
ℹ Start R with `pixi run R`, or see https://roald-arboel.com/rpix/articles/ide.html.
```

Your usual R can't use the environment's packages: they're built for the environment's R, and loading them can crash another R. So rpix doesn't try; start the environment's R instead, as above.

## Check

In the IDE's R console, `R.home()` should be inside the project's `.pixi/envs/` folder:

```r
R.home()
#> [1] "/path/to/project/.pixi/envs/default/lib/R"
```
